newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman inaugurated as Nicaraguan president.
newsitem.headline: Aleman inaugurated as Nicaraguan president.

text.p: Right-winger Arnoldo Aleman was sworn in as president of Nicaragua on Friday in what was billed as the first democratic, peaceful transfer of power in the country's modern history.
In a ceremony attended by seven Latin American presidents and delegations from 61 countries, Aleman replaced outgoing President Violeta Chamorro, who ended a nearly seven-year term in office.

Aleman received the presidential sash from the newly-elected president of the National Assembly, Liberal Ivan Escobar Fornos, in a peaceful ceremony witnessed by Chamorro and top army officials, but boycotted by the left-wing Sandinista Front.

The beefy Aleman, dressed in a dark suit, received the sash adorned with Nicaragua's blue-and-white colors and smiled and waved to the crowd. A mass of blue-and-white balloons were released into the air.

Aleman, a 50-year-old lawyer and coffee grower, began his five-year term amid a political crisis sparked by threats of street protests from the Sandinistas and the killing of six soldiers by unidentified gunmen in rural Nicaragua Thursday.
He easily beat former Sandinista president Daniel Ortega in elections Oct. 20. The Sandinistas claimed the voting was fraudulent and have refused to recognize his government.
